label: Diagram 2.1
caption: Diagram 2.1 Maximum length of ramp at a given gradient
description: The drawing is a line chart with the title Diagram 2.1, Maximum length of ramp at a given gradient shown in a green bar along the bottom. The vertical axis is labelled Gradient of ramp and runs from 1:10 at the bottom to 1:20 at the top, with a vertical arrow on the left marked shallower at the top and steeper at the bottom. The horizontal axis is labelled Maximum length of ramp flight (m) and is marked 0 to 10. A straight diagonal line of black dots rises from left to right, and a continuous grey shaded area fills the region between this line and the horizontal axis, with a vertical line dropping from each dot to the axis. The dots are numbered, reading 83, 166, 231, 286, 333, 375, 412, 444, 474 and 500 from left to right, the last marked Rise (mm) 500, while the first dot, above 0, has no number. A legend at lower right shows a grey square labelled does not comply and a white square labelled satisfactory. A Notes box at upper right reads: 1. Gradient x length of flight = rise e.g. 1/20 x 10 = 500mm. 2. A site gradient of 1:15 will usually require a series of ramps of 1:12 interspersed with landings where necessary.
